I can't recommend an i3 before the 8th generation at this point unless you just have to save the money. Four cores is pretty much the least I would take and i3 was 2 core until the 8th generation. That is just me though and a lot of people seem to be fine with 2 cores (really depends on the games as they are using more and more threads now).

What I can say is that you will care some about hard drive sizes. Many games today can take up 60+ GB, especially once you add patches and such. BF1 with everything currently takes up 79.3 GB. Doom is 67 GB. Hell, Lego games take up 15-20 GB now.

So here is my suggestion.

1) Ryzen 5 1600 or i5 8600K. I am a little partial to the Ryzen myself as it can overclock to meet the speeds of the i5. You can go with another CPU and replace it later with a better one though. Gaming tends to like higher clock speeds and 2-4 cores so keep that in mind.

2) At least 16 GB ram. Folks say you don't need that much but I disagree. You can do 8 now and add more later though if money is an issue. Do not go below 8.

3) 256 GB SSD + 1 TB Hard Drive at minimum if you are going to have a lot of games available. With Steam and Origin it is easy to move games from drive to drive instead of having to uninstall/reinstall. If you realize you are not playing a game as often you can move it to your slower hard drive.

4) Build for now with an eye to upgrade in pieces later. Can't afford the SSD+HD, maybe get large HD and deal with the slower load times then upgrade later. Can't afford a new video card, maybe go with something used (like an R9 390) and upgrade later. Maybe just do 8GB Ram now and add some more later. Building it yourself means you can find ways to cut corners some now but allow you to add on later. Buying pre-built may not be the same.
